newsitem.title: JAPAN: Paperback-sized video camera to buoy JVC earnings.
newsitem.headline: Paperback-sized video camera to buoy JVC earnings.

text.p: Audio and video equipment maker Victor Co of Japan Ltd (JVC) is expected to see its earnings for the business year to next March buoyed by its slick paperback-sized digital video cameras.
JVC launched the world's smallest and lightest digital video camera, the GR-DV1, last December, and has since been enjoying robust sales.

"The hit product will help JVC's performance to further improve this fiscal year, as it came back to profitability in terms of operating revenue last year after extensive efforts to restructure itself," said Yoshiharu Izumi, an analyst at UBS Securities Ltd.

The video cameras, introduced last autumn, use digital technology and are smaller and lighter than analog-format camcorders. Images captured with the cameras can be viewed and edited on computer screens.
JVC's GR-DV1 is about half the size of the company's older analog video camera and weighs 450 grams, compared with 820 grams for the analog camcorder.
Less than a month after launching the GR-DV1, JVC decided to raise output from 10,000 per month to 15,000 as a backlog of orders from shops piled up.
Since then, it has raised monthly production twice to the current level of 30,000 to catch up with demand, a spokesman for the company said.
JVC expects to have sold 170,000 units of the GR-DV1 by the end of September, 50,000 of them overseas, the spokesman said.
"The success of JVC's new product can mainly be attributed to the fact that it focused on delivering to market the smallest digital camcorder as early as possible," said Izumi.
Riding the boom, the company plans to launch a new version equipped with a larger liquid crystal display (LCD) colour monitor on October 1.
"We are aiming this new addition to the lineup at family users, since the LCD monitor enables clear viewing of the subject for worry-free recording," said the spokesman.
Nevertheless, the competition is expected to heat up as other big-name audiovisual manufacturers follow JVC's lead, they said.
Sony Corp plans to introduce on September 10 a digital video camera with an LCD monitor that will be slightly smaller and lighter than JVC's comparable product.
As for the long-term outlook for JVC, analysts said it depends on whether it can continue to make hit products.

Joseph Osha, an analyst at Merrill Lynch Japan Inc, said JVC's profitability depends on pricing of audio equipment components that it purchases from group companies of Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd.

As of the end of March, Matsushita Electric Industrial owned 52.4 percent of JVC. Osha said Matsushita was unlikely to let JVC's profitability rise sharply by supplying components at low prices from other group companies, as it put priority on the profitability of the component makers.
